clue.text: Damn this puzzle?

definitions.meaning: an oath such as damn is an angry utterance, a word said when annoyed
the very grid of clues and lights the solver is working on

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first word as a phrase: an expletive is a word spoken in a temper, a cross word.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry expletive is literally a bad-tempered word, and the grid being solved is itself a word puzzle of this kind.

clue.text: A song may be something desirable

definitions.meaning: a round for several voices, often humorous, sung in turn
a good prospect, especially an eligible partner

explanation.definitionFit: A round sung by several voices bears this name, and an eligible partner worth landing is called a good one.

clue.text: Chaps at the top in charge of cricket ground

parts.note: over means having authority above, in charge of
Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Men at the top running a cricket venue.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London ground known as the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulers holding supreme power over others are the men at the very top.

clue.text: Youths multiplying in centre of Brussels

indicators.note: in means the word for multiplying sits inside the central letters
centre of means take the middle letters of the word Brussels

parts.note: multiplying by three is tripling

explanation.surface: Young people breeding fast in the heart of the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'multiplying' looks like the definition's verb, but it is fodder; 'centre of' picks the two middle letters of the eight-letter capital's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Young lads not yet fully grown are traditionally called by this word.

clue.text: Given short measure after love letter

indicators.note: after places the short measure following the love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a micron is a tiny unit of length, a millionth of a metre

explanation.surface: Someone shortchanged following a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given short measure' looks like being cheated; here 'short measure' is a tiny length.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the characters of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Clubs for road-users

definitions.meaning: golf clubs used for long shots off the tee
people at the wheel of cars

explanation.definitionFit: Long-hitting golf woods share their name with motorists at the wheel.

clue.text: Muslim paper about Iran's borders

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: about means the border letters of Iran are turned round
borders means the first and last letters of Iran

explanation.surface: A Muslim newspaper reporting on Iranian frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' gives IN, the first and last letters of IRAN, and 'about' turns it to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the larger of Islam's two main branches is a Muslim.

clue.text: Fielder may be Freudian?

definitions.meaning: a close catching position beside the wicketkeeper in cricket
a small error of speech revealing a hidden thought

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips stand beside the wicketkeeper; a Freudian slip is a revealing verbal error.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket catching position shares its name with a small mistake that, in psychoanalytic terms, betrays the unconscious.

clue.text: Idea one rejected as unacceptable

indicators.note: rejected means the one is thrown out of the idea

parts.note: an idea is a notion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A suggestion turned down as out of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, behaviour that simply will not do is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Angry northern worker going under in excavation

indicators.note: in a down entry, going under puts the northern worker below the in-excavation part

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
the ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A northern labourer furious at being sent down into a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling resentment at unfair treatment is a form of being angry.

clue.text: Leader of Trojans succeeding one belonging to them

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of Trojans

parts.note: an heir is one who succeeds to a title or estate

explanation.surface: A Trojan chief's successor owns it all.
explanation.definitionFit: This possessive word refers to things owned by several people.

clue.text: Dietitian in a stew set in motion

indicators.note: in a stew means flustered and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nutritionist flustered about getting something started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' suits a dietitian's kitchen but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something begun or launched has been started off.

clue.text: Hotel employee providing everyone with drink after hours

indicators.note: after places everyone with drink following the hours

parts.note: all means everyone
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A hotel worker serving everybody a drink after closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman or concierge in a hotel's entrance hall is one of its staff.

clue.text: Problem with horse on seafront

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the horse follows

parts.note: the front of sea is its first letter S
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Trouble with a horse down by the promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch or unforeseen difficulty is a problem.

clue.text: Feeble desire? Say why that's wrong

parts.note: a wish is a desire

indicators.note: that's wrong says the letters of say why are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A weak longing and a demand to know why it is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insipid and lacking firmness or resolve is weak.

clue.text: Napier's wild cat

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An untamed feline belonging to Napier.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of Napier's is a letter of the fodder, not just a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-haired breed of domestic feline.

clue.text: Source of interest for head

definitions.meaning: the capital sum on which interest is earned
the person in charge, such as of a school

explanation.definitionFit: The capital sum lent or invested earns interest, and a school's chief is its leader.

clue.text: Philosopher from Spain possibly touring Australia

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the Spanish letters surround Australia
possibly signals that Spain could be arranged another way

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker from Spain on a tour of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the country to SPINA before 'touring' wraps it round the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker.

clue.text: In the words of the poet: "Order a drink"

indicators.note: In means the order and a are placed inside the poet's words

parts.note: a poet's words make an ode, a lyric poem
to range is to set in order, arrange

explanation.surface: Quoting a poet: a request for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Order a drink' look like the poet's line, but 'In the words of the poet' is a container: the poem holds the order and the a.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetened soft beverage made with citrus juice.

clue.text: Location of tavern is audible and visible

indicators.note: is audible means the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: a tavern is an inn and its location is its site

explanation.surface: The pub's position can be heard and seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within view can be seen.

clue.text: Mean to carry on this evening

indicators.note: to carry means the mean word holds the on within it

parts.note: tight means mean, stingy

explanation.surface: Intending to keep going tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like intend, but it is stingy, giving TIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: It refers to the evening or night of the present day.

clue.text: Articles requiring skill, basically

parts.note: the indefinite article
the definite article
art is skill

explanation.surface: Objects that demand craft, fundamentally.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'Articles' gives both grammar articles, A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentally, in one's true nature, is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Silly redhead getting stuck

indicators.note: silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daft ginger-haired person getting glued.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that clung fast has stuck.

clue.text: Potter's material provided by Ali originally

definitions.meaning: the earth a potter shapes on the wheel

explanation.definitionFit: Earth used for pottery shares its name with the boxer Muhammad Ali's birth surname.

clue.text: Like constant cold jelly

parts.note: as means like
pi is the mathematical constant
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Like a steady chilled jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatine made from meat stock is a jelly.

clue.text: Where AA members may be taken for a ride?

definitions.text: Where AA members may be taken for a ride?

parts.words: Where AA members may be taken for a ride?
parts.note: AA suggests the motoring Automobile Association, but its members here are from Alcoholics Anonymous, who abstain from drink, as if riding a cart

explanation.walkthrough: The AA is both Britain's motoring breakdown service and Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from alcohol is idiomatically described as riding a water cart.

clue.text: Drain off lowest part

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drain away the very bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of greatest depression is the lowest point.

clue.text: Girl likely to lose heart

indicators.note: to lose heart means the middle letters of likely are removed

explanation.surface: A girl probably going to be discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, from the flower.

clue.text: Performer for whom nippers go crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A star that sends youngsters wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart vocalist is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Small solid fragment of pottery

parts.note: hard means solid

explanation.surface: A tiny firm piece of broken crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp broken piece of a pot or glass.

clue.text: Fortunate girl holding high card

indicators.note: holding means the girl contains the card

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name
K is king, a high playing card

explanation.surface: A lucky woman with a strong card in her hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being favoured by good fortune.

clue.text: Toy boy's stomach

parts.note: Teddy is a boy's name
to stomach is to bear, tolerate

explanation.surface: A plaything that is a lad's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' looks like a noun but is the verb, to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed plaything shaped like an animal.
